```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
here::i_am("errata.qmd")

disatt <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "text_disattenuation.csv"),
                   show_col_types = FALSE)
f3 <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "figure_3_robustness.csv"),
               show_col_types = FALSE)
f2 <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "figure_2_standardized_tes_annotations.csv"),
               show_col_types = FALSE)

jerit <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "text_jerit_sensitivity.csv"),
                  show_col_types = FALSE)

d <- function(pattern) disatt$value[str_detect(disatt$quantity, pattern)]
j <- function(pattern) jerit$value[str_detect(jerit$quantity, pattern)]
r2 <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)
r3 <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x)

n_pairs <- f2$value[f2$quantity == "pooled treatment effect pairs"]
medians <- f3$median
subsets <- f3 |> filter(n_used != n_pairs)
capped <- subsets |>
  filter(n_used < n_pairs, n_evaluated < n_combinations) |>
  filter(n_used == max(n_used))
smallest_capped <- n_pairs - capped$n_used
uncapped <- subsets |>
  filter(n_used < n_pairs, n_used == capped$n_used + 1)
comma <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)

# spell: the errata quote sentences that spell their numbers out, and a corrected
# sentence has to spell the computed replacement out too rather than printing a
# numeral where the article printed a word.
spell <- function(n) {
  words <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight",
             "nine", "ten", "eleven", "twelve")
  stopifnot(n >= 1, n <= length(words), n == round(n))
  words[n]
}
```

```{r entries}
# THE ERRATA SPINE. Every entry is defined once, here, and rendered from here: into this
# document, and into whatever else needs it, which reads the errata_entries.csv written at
# the bottom of this file rather than keeping a second hand-typed copy.
#
# [[...]] marks the span that changes, on both sides. Each renderer supplies its own markup
# for it, and this document's convention is to bold the corrected side only, so the marks
# on the published side are stripped rather than set. Nothing else in a field is markup.
#
# Numbering is the published note's and is APPEND-ONLY: an entry can already have been
# cited, so a later finding is added at the end and never interleaved.
#
# claim_ids names the ground-truth rows an entry corrects, semicolon-separated, so that
# "is this finding published?" is a query rather than a judgment. It is empty where the
# entry has no ground-truth row: entry 3 is the definition that CAUSES three of the wrong
# values below, and a cause sentence carries no number of its own. Every id listed here is
# checked against the ground truth by build_ground_truth.R.
entries <- tribble(
  ~entry, ~class, ~source, ~form, ~title, ~location, ~published, ~corrected, ~note, ~claim_ids,
  ~corrected_values, ~values_in_spans,

  1, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The disattenuated correlation",
  "published, main text",
  "The disattenuated correlation is found to be $[[0.64]]/\\sqrt{[[0.78]]*[[0.82]]} = [[0.80]]$, further attesting to the strength of lab-field correspondence in published work.",
  str_c("The disattenuated correlation is found to be $[[", r2(d("^raw Pearson")),
        "]]/\\sqrt{[[", r2(d("^lab reliability$")), "]]*[[", r2(d("^field reliability$")),
        "]]} = [[", r2(d("^disattenuated correlation$")),
        "]]$, further attesting to the strength of lab-field correspondence in published work."),
  str_glue(
    "Three separate errors move this number. The two reliabilities are squared, which item ",
    "3 sets out. The raw Pearson correlation of 0.64 is {r2(d('^raw Pearson'))} once the ",
    "Gneezy and Rustichini (2004) female treatment effect is standardized by its own ",
    "control group rather than by a male treatment group, as Equation 1 of the article ",
    "requires. And the List (2006) field standard error, which enters the reliability ",
    "simulation, is read from the lab vector in the deposited script."),
  "disc_disatt_numerator;disc_disatt_lab;disc_disatt_field;disc_disattenuated",
  str_c(r2(d("^raw Pearson")), ";", r2(d("^lab reliability$")), ";",
        r2(d("^field reliability$")), ";", r2(d("^disattenuated correlation$"))), TRUE,

  2, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The two reliabilities",
  "published, main text",
  "The reliabilities for the lab and field treatment effects are [[0.78]] and [[0.82]], respectively.",
  str_glue("The reliabilities for the lab and field treatment effects are [[{r2(d('^lab reliability$'))}]] and [[{r2(d('^field reliability$'))}]], respectively."),
  str_glue(
    "A correlation near 0.9 is much larger than its own square, which is why correcting the ",
    "definition in item 3 moves these two values so far. Keeping the squared definition and ",
    "fixing only the indexing gives {r2(d('^lab reliability, squared'))} and ",
    "{r2(d('^field reliability, squared'))}, which is why the published pair is so close to ",
    "what the corrected code produces under the article's own definition."),
  "disc_lab_reliability;disc_field_reliability",
  str_c(r2(d("^lab reliability$")), ";", r2(d("^field reliability$"))), TRUE,

  3, "definition", "pipeline", "full",
  "The definition of the reliability",
  "published, footnote 7",
  "The estimated reliability is [[the square of the correlation]] between two treatment effect draws.",
  "The estimated reliability is [[the correlation]] between two treatment effect draws.",
  paste(
    "The reliability of a measure is the correlation between two parallel measurements of",
    "it, and Spearman's correction for attenuation divides the observed correlation by the",
    "geometric mean of the two reliabilities. Squaring the correlations first makes the",
    "denominator too small and the corrected estimate too large. The deposited script",
    "implements the footnote exactly as written, so the article and its code agree with each",
    "other and both depart from the correction they invoke. The error was identified by",
    "David Broockman (UC Berkeley)."),
  "", NA_character_, NA,

  4, "description", "pipeline", "full",
  "The median correlation across permutations",
  "published, main text",
  "Unsurprisingly, the median correlation [[stays constant]] across all permutations.",
  str_glue("Unsurprisingly, the median correlation [[stays between {r2(min(medians))} and {r2(max(medians))}]] across all permutations."),
  str_glue(
    "Figure 3 itself is right and is not reprinted here. Its median series takes ",
    "{length(unique(round(medians, 2)))} distinct values at two decimal places across the ",
    "{nrow(f3)} combination sizes, running from {r3(min(medians))} to {r3(max(medians))}. ",
    "The deposited code gives the same answer at its own random draw, from 0.720 to 0.729, ",
    "so this is a description that neither run supports rather than a number the pipeline ",
    "has moved."),
  "results_median_constant", NA_character_, NA,

  5, "definition", "pipeline", "full",
  "The note to Figure 3",
  "published, note to Figure 3",
  "*Note*: we calculate the rank-order correlations of the 21 treatment effect pairs included in the meta-analysis, under [[all possible combinations]] duplicating or removing any 1, 2, 3... or 10 of them.",
  str_glue("*Note*: we calculate the rank-order correlations of the 21 treatment effect pairs included in the meta-analysis, under [[all possible combinations, sampled down to {comma(max(subsets$n_evaluated))} wherever more exist,]] duplicating or removing any 1, 2, 3... or 10 of them."),
  str_glue(
    "The note and footnote 6 contradict each other, and footnote 6 is the one the code ",
    "follows: {comma(sum(subsets$n_evaluated))} of the {comma(sum(subsets$n_combinations))} ",
    "available combinations were evaluated. Again the figure is right; only its note ",
    "overstates what was computed."),
  "fig3_note_all_combinations", NA_character_, NA,

  6, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The subset size at which sampling begins",
  "published, footnote 6",
  "When dropping more than any [[six]] pairs, we randomly sampled 50,000 of the possible combinations.",
  str_glue("When dropping more than any [[{spell(smallest_capped - 1)}]] pairs, we randomly sampled {comma(max(subsets$n_evaluated))} of the possible combinations."),
  str_glue(
    "Dropping {spell(smallest_capped)} of the {n_pairs} pairs leaves ",
    "{comma(capped$n_combinations)} combinations, which is already above the cap, so the ",
    "sampling applies there too; dropping {spell(smallest_capped - 1)} leaves ",
    "{comma(uncapped$n_combinations)}, which is below it. The deposited code applies the ",
    "same cap by the same test, so this is a description of the code rather than a change ",
    "to it. The footnote is also silent on the duplication side of the exercise, where the ",
    "cap binds at exactly the same point."),
  "fn6_cap_threshold", as.character(smallest_capped), FALSE,

  7, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The range of pooled correlations across the Jerit candidate pairs",
  "published, footnote 5",
  "Which pair we included caused slight changes in the overall correlation, ranging from [[0.699]] to [[0.762]].",
  str_glue(
    "Which pair we included caused slight changes in the overall correlation, ranging from ",
    "[[{r3(j('^minimum'))}]] to [[{r3(j('^maximum'))}]]."),
  str_glue(
    "Both endpoints move for the reason set out in item 1: the Gneezy and Rustichini (2004) ",
    "female treatment effect is standardized by a male treatment group rather than by its ",
    "own control group, and correcting it shifts every pooled correlation. The lower ",
    "endpoint is doubly wrong, because the deposited script prints ",
    "{sprintf('%.7f', 0.6995778219)} and the footnote sets it down as 0.699, truncating ",
    "where the three decimals it uses would round to 0.700. The claim the footnote makes ",
    "is unaffected: which Jerit pair is included still moves the pooled correlation only ",
    "slightly, over a range of {r3(j('^maximum') - j('^minimum'))} rather than the ",
    "published {r3(0.7619357336 - 0.6995778219)}."),
  "fn5_min;fn5_max",
  str_c(r3(j("^minimum")), ";", r3(j("^maximum"))), TRUE,

  8, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The raw Pearson correlation, where the Discussion states it on its own",
  "published, main text",
  "The raw Pearson correlation among the 21 treatment effect pairs is [[0.64]].",
  str_glue(
    "The raw Pearson correlation among the 21 treatment effect pairs is ",
    "[[{r2(d('^raw Pearson'))}]]."),
  str_glue(
    "The same quantity as the numerator item 1 corrects, stated here as a sentence of its ",
    "own two sentences earlier, and moved by the same standardization correction. It is ",
    "listed separately because a reader quoting this sentence would not be reading the ",
    "formula, and the two would otherwise disagree in a corrected edition."),
  "disc_raw_pearson", r2(d("^raw Pearson")), TRUE
) |>
  mutate(across(c(title, published, corrected, note, claim_ids, corrected_values), as.character))

stopifnot(nrow(entries) == max(entries$entry), !anyDuplicated(entries$entry))

# Gate: corrected_values agrees with the sentence it was glued into ----
# The column and the sentence are written from one expression, so they begin in agreement
# and this gate exists for the edit that separates them: a value moved from one marked span
# to another, a span reworded to carry a second number, a claim id appended without its
# value. Each value has to be inside the span it belongs to, matched by position where the
# counts line up, and the spelled form counts as the numeral because entry 5 sets "four".
marked_spans <- function(x) str_match_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]")[[1]][, 2]

inside_span <- function(value, span) {
  numeral <- str_detect(span, fixed(value))
  spelled <- !is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(value))) &&
    as.numeric(value) %in% seq_len(12) &&
    str_detect(span, fixed(spell(as.numeric(value))))
  numeral || spelled
}

# values_in_spans is FALSE where the claim's scale is not the sentence's, which happens
# whenever the sentence states a threshold and the extraction records the first value past
# it. Entry 6 is the corpus's first: the footnote says sampling begins when more than any
# five pairs are dropped, and the claim it corrects is the smallest number of dropped pairs
# at which the cap binds, which is six. Both are right and neither is the other. THE COLUMN
# IS ALWAYS ON THE CLAIM'S SCALE, because a claims file can only assert against the claim
# it computes; the flag records where that parts company with the printed token, and the
# note beside it has to say why.
quantified <- entries |>
  filter(!is.na(corrected_values), values_in_spans) |>
  mutate(ids = str_split(claim_ids, ";"), values = str_split(corrected_values, ";"),
         spans = map(corrected, marked_spans))

stopifnot(all(lengths(quantified$ids) == lengths(quantified$values)))

# Where a span carries two numbers at once the pairing by position is not available, so the
# value is required to be inside some span instead. No entry here is of that shape; the
# branch is what keeps the gate usable on a paper that has one.
value_placed <- pmap_lgl(quantified, function(...) {
  e <- list(...)
  if (length(e$values) == length(e$spans)) {
    all(map2_lgl(e$values, e$spans, inside_span))
  } else {
    all(map_lgl(e$values, \(v) any(map_lgl(e$spans, \(s) inside_span(v, s)))))
  }
})

if (!all(value_placed)) {
  print(quantified |> filter(!value_placed) |> select(entry, title, corrected_values, corrected))
  stop("An entry's corrected_values are not in the spans of its corrected sentence.")
}

# An entry that changes a quantity has to say which one, and an entry that changes none
# may not carry a value. The class is the declaration and this is where it binds.
stopifnot(
  all(!is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$class == "quantity"])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$class != "quantity"])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values) | !is.na(entries$claim_ids)),
  all(!is.na(entries$values_in_spans[!is.na(entries$corrected_values)])),
  all(is.na(entries$values_in_spans[is.na(entries$corrected_values)])),
  all(str_length(entries$note[!replace_na(entries$values_in_spans, TRUE)]) > 0)
)

# The spine's markup, resolved for this document. Bold means ** in prose and \mathbf{} in
# math, which is why the resolver splits on the math delimiter rather than substituting
# blindly: entry 1's changed spans are all inside $...$.
bold <- function(x) {
  pieces <- str_split_1(x, fixed("$"))
  in_math <- seq_along(pieces) %% 2 == 0
  pieces[in_math] <- str_replace_all(pieces[in_math], "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]", "\\\\mathbf{\\1}")
  pieces[!in_math] <- str_replace_all(pieces[!in_math], "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]", "**\\1**")
  str_flatten(pieces, "$")
}

# This note bolds the corrected side only, so the published side is set with its marks
# removed rather than resolved.
plain <- function(x) str_remove_all(x, "\\[\\[|\\]\\]")

# A heading is only a heading when a blank line precedes it, which is why every emitted
# entry opens with one.
emit <- function(n) {
  e <- entries |> filter(entry == n)
  cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\n> ", plain(e$published),
      "\n\nCorrected:\n\n> ", bold(e$corrected), "\n\n", e$note, "\n", sep = "")
}
```

This note lists `r spell(nrow(entries))` misstated claims in "Assessing the Correspondence between Experimental Results Obtained in the Lab and Field: A Review of Recent Social Science Research," published in *Political Science Research and Methods* 3(1), 113--131, doi [10.1017/psrm.2014.10](https://doi.org/10.1017/psrm.2014.10). **None of them changes a conclusion of the article.** The rank-order correlation of `r r2(f2$value[f2$quantity == "pooled Spearman rho, 21 pairs"])` that the abstract leads with is unaffected, and the disattenuated correlation still exceeds the raw one, so the finding that lab-field correspondence is strong stands. Each item is recorded because a reader who quoted the sentence would be quoting a claim the article's own data do not support.

The first three concern one calculation and share one cause. The last three are descriptions of the robustness exercise behind Figure 3, whose numbers are themselves correct.

Every corrected value below is computed from the deposited data at the time this document is rendered; bold marks the tokens that change. The code and output supporting each correction are at [github.com/active-maintenance-aec/coppock_green_2015](https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/coppock_green_2015).

```{r rendered-entries, results="asis"}
walk(entries$entry, emit)
```

```{r emit-spine}
# The machine-readable spine, written wherever this document is rendered. Anything else
# that needs these entries reads it rather than keeping its own copy, so the two cannot
# drift.
write_csv(entries, here("errata_entries.csv"))
```
